def: The PCIe packet that carries a request (memory, I/O, configuration, message) or a completion between two PCIe functions. Its header (3 or 4 DWORDs in non-Flit mode) says what kind of packet it is, who sent it and where it goes.

The PCIe completion TLP that returns data for a non-posted read request. It echoes the requester's Requester ID and Tag and carries Byte Count and Lower Address so the requester can reassemble split completions.

The PCIe link mode introduced with the 64 GT/s generation in which TLPs and DLLPs are packed into fixed-size flits protected by CRC and forward error correction, with a different TLP header format from non-Flit mode.
One 64-byte NVMe command in a Submission Queue: opcode, flags and Command Identifier in Dword 0, the namespace, metadata and data pointers, and command-specific Dwords 10 to 15.
The 16-byte record an NVMe controller writes into a Completion Queue when a command finishes: command-specific result, SQ Head Pointer, SQ Identifier, Command Identifier, Phase Tag and Status Field.
Bit 16 of CQE Dword 3. The controller inverts the value it writes each time it wraps around the Completion Queue, so the host can tell new entries from old ones without the queue ever being cleared.
A 64-bit pointer to a location inside one memory page, used by NVMe over PCIe to describe where a command's data lives. PRP1 may have an offset; every later data entry is page aligned.

An array of 8-byte page-aligned PRP entries in host memory, pointed to by PRP2 when a transfer touches more than two memory pages. When more entries remain than fit in the list page, its last slot points to the next list page.
The per-function register space (256 bytes for PCI, 4 KiB for PCIe) holding identity, BARs, command/status, and the capability lists through which software discovers and configures a PCIe function.
In any stable system, the average number of items inside (L) equals the arrival rate (λ) times the average time each item spends inside (W). For storage: commands in flight = IOPS × average latency.
An SSD endurance rating: how many times the drive's full user capacity may be written per day over the warranty period. TBW = DWPD × capacity × 365 × years.
